s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC followed by 3060 cGY at the neck and mediastinum
Left upper eyelid mass excised on 3 separate occasions
Painless proptosis developed four months later
Left-sided facial numbness developed seventeen months later
Histopathology showed multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI showed lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Genetic testing revealed a splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, positive for CD68, and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme, are characteristic of Erdheim-Chester disease

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology showing multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, with positive CD68 immunohistochemistry, is also consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of proptosis, facial numbness, and histopathology showing osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells, although Langerhans cell histiocytosis typically has positive S100 and CD1a staining

shortlist.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive clinical course and histopathology showing a proliferation of mononuclear cells with increased mitotic activity, which could be seen in histiocytic sarcoma

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells in the histopathology, although the clinical presentation and other histopathological features are not typical for giant cell tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a painless, left upper eyelid mass, proptosis, and later left-sided facial numbness, combined with histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, and immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease. The involvement of the orbit and extension into the intracranial compartment also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with lymphadenopathy and is positive for S100, which is not seen in this case

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with a different immunohistochemical profile, including positivity for CD1a and S100

rejected.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and different histopathological features

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Typically presents with a distinct histopathological appearance and is usually positive for RANKL
